newsitem.title: GERMANY: Puma shares jump on takeover talk, but group is mum.
newsitem.headline: Puma shares jump on takeover talk, but group is mum.

text.p: Shares in German sportswear maker Puma AG continued to soar in late afternoon trading in Frankfurt even after Italian clothing giant Benetton had denied market talk it was interested in acquiring the German group.
By 1421 GMT Puma shares, traded on the electronic IBIS DAX system, were the session's biggest gainers rising 5.16 percent to 55 marks, reflecting a jump from the 54.90 mark bourse close.

Analysts said talk that Italian fashion group Benetton might be considering snapping up the southern German group was the only reason for the sharp price jump. Puma posted slightly disappointing results on Friday, prompting several banks to downgrade their recommendations.
Benetton, however, said it was not interested. When asked about the market talk in Germany, a spokeswoman said "This is not true."

Similarly Puma officials brushed off the talk. Puma chief financial officer Dieter Bock told Reuters "We think that this talk is solely based on rumours," adding "our company has nothing to substantiate such talk."

Monday's share price rise, which surprised many dealers, occurred despite news that U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs and German bank Commerzbank both downgraded the group's shares after Friday's half-year results.
Commerzbank put Puma on hold, having had them on buy, while Goldman Sachs labelled the shares a market performer.

Even though the market talk has been denied, analysts said the suggestion Benetton could be eyeing Puma was not entirely ludicrous and might still be able to drive the share price higher for a short while.
"It cannot be those numbers pushing the Puma shares," a dealer said. Another analyst added "This is not wholly implausible," noting that there was often a kernel of truth to such rumours.
Dealers said they were unsure where Puma shares might head from here, having had their earlier predictions of a dip in prices on an official denial proved wrong.
